data.narrative:
Quantum Brilliance is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Andrew Horsley, Marcus Doherty, and Mark Luo, having raised $50M+ to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public comps (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method. Using the $50M total raised as a proxy base valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier for Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $100M. Peer-median analysis is not applicable due to insufficient narrow comparables: while 6 same-sector peers exist, none meet the threshold of three or more datapoints within the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier. Broadening to all-sector median peers would lack meaningful precision.

The triangulated valuation range is $85M to $115M, with a median of $100M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty. The primary limitations are the nascent state of the quantum computing sector and lack of sufficiently comparable Series A valuations in the same development phase. Key uncertainties include product maturity relative to peers, go-to-market timing, and capital efficiency relative to the broader comp set. Additional funding rounds and revenue inflection would materially refine this range.
